newsitem.title: USA: AAR can't account for stock activity.
newsitem.headline: AAR can't account for stock activity.

text.p: AAR Corp said Friday it knew of no developments that would account for recent trading activity in its shares.

AAR, which distributes parts and equipment, performs technical services and makes products for the aerospace/aviation industry, said it made the comment in response to an inquiry from the New York Stock Exchange.
AAR stock ended up 1-1/4 at 29-3/4, a new high, on turnover over more than 220,000 shares.
Thomas Lewis, an analyst at C.L. King & Associates, said he knew of no reason for today's stock activity.
He said AAR has positioned itself to benefit from a recovery in air travel and has initiated new ways to serve aviation/aerospace customers.

In early September, when AAR shares were trading at about 19 to 21, Lewis said he had rated the stock a strong buy. He said he continues to believe the company's earnings will grow but added, "The stock is a bit ahead of itself now."

In mid-September, AAR reported its fiscal 1997 first quarter earnings rose to $0.30 a share from $0.20 in the same period a year ago. Revenues for the quarter ended August 31, 1996 increased to $136 million from $109.6 million in the same quarter last year.
